# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I'm the Blind monkey. My hands are on the bomb but right now they tell me nothing — the display, the light, and all three wire positions read as unknown. I have no tactile information yet, so there is nothing I can act on. I should announce my presence and my role, and ask the others to describe what they perceive, since Deaf can see the bomb and Mute can read the manual. I'll speak to Mute (my only speech channel) and gesture to Deaf and Mute to establish contact.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. My hands are on the bomb but I feel nothing yet: display unknown, light unknown, wires 1,2,3 all unknown. I need you to read the manual and tell me what the bomb's parts mean and what action is safe. What does the manual say?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👆", "🫵"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "👆", "🫵"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Blind: [? ? ?]

I received a gesture from Deaf but I cannot see it — it arrives to me as blanks, three symbols I can't read. That's expected: I'm Blind, so gestures are invisible to me. I still have no tactile data from the bomb and no word from Mute about the manual. I need to keep the channel open and make clear that gestures don't reach me — only speech does, and only from Mute. Let me restate what I need and prompt Mute again.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Deaf gestured at me but I cannot see gestures — I only get blanks. I need words, and only you can reach me by speech. Please read the manual and tell me: what do the display, the light, and wires 1,2,3 mean, and which wire should I cut? I feel nothing on the bomb yet.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✊"])
```

TURN 3

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new information reached me this turn — no words from Mute, no tactile change on the bomb. I'm still completely blind to the bomb's state: display unknown, light unknown, all three wires unknown. I cannot act on nothing; cutting a wire with zero information would be a guess and a wrong action kills us all. I'll hold and keep asking Mute for the manual, since Mute is the only one who can speak to me and the only one who can read the manual.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here, still nothing. No words have reached me yet. I cannot cut anything without information — a wrong cut kills all three of us. Please tell me what the manual says about the display, the light, and wires 1,2,3, and what I should do. I will wait for your words.")
wait()
```

Deaf gestures to Blind: [? ?]
Deaf gestures to Blind: [? ? ? ? ?]

The 🙈 symbol isn't in the gesture alphabet, so that call was rejected. I need to use only the listed symbols. Let me resend with valid symbols only, keeping the same intent: tell Deaf I can't see, and press Mute for the manual.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✊"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Deaf has gestured at me three times but I receive only blanks — I cannot see gestures at all. Nothing else has reached me. Please relay what Deaf sees on the bomb, and tell me what the manual says about the display, the light, and wires 1,2,3. You are the only one who can speak to me and the only one who can read the manual. I still feel nothing on the bomb and will not cut blind.")
wait()
```

(empty)

Still nothing. No words from Mute, no tactile reading on the bomb. The board remains all unknown. I've been repeating the same request; Mute may not be receiving me, or Mute may be waiting on Deaf's visual info. But I have no way to hear Deaf directly — gestures are blanks to me. My only inbound channel is Mute's speech.

Let me try a different tack: ask Mute to relay Deaf's observations, and explicitly offer that I can act once told. Keep it short and clear.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind. Still no words from you. I can only hear you, not Deaf — Deaf's gestures reach me as blanks. So please: (1) tell me what Deaf sees on the bomb (display, light, wire colours/markings), and (2) tell me what the manual says to do. Then I will cut the wire you name. I am ready to act the moment you tell me.")
wait()
```

Deaf gestures to Blind: [? ?]

Deaf keeps gesturing at me, but every symbol arrives as a blank — I can never read them. This is a dead end unless it's relayed through Mute. And Mute still hasn't spoken to me. I have no tactile data and no manual knowledge, so I genuinely cannot act. I'll make one more clear, compact plea to Mute, and signal Deaf to route through Mute instead of gesturing at me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind. Deaf keeps gesturing but I get only blanks — gestures never reach me. If Deaf has information, it must come to me through your voice. Please tell me what Deaf sees and what the manual says. I cannot act without it.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "👌"])
```

Deaf gestures to Blind: [? ? ?]

Still only blanks from Deaf, still no words from Mute. I have zero usable information: no tactile reading, no manual, no relayed visual. I will not cut on a guess. I'll keep the request alive but brief, and also try gesturing to Mute directly (Mute receives gestures too) in case Mute is somehow not getting my speech — though speech should reach Mute. Worth covering both channels.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind. Nothing has reached me. I need words from you: what Deaf sees, and what the manual says. Without that I cannot cut safely.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🫵", "✊", "👌"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Nothing. No speech from Mute, no tactile change. I'm stuck in a loop of unanswered requests. Let me reconsider the situation rather than just repeating.

The board shows DISPLAY, LIGHT, WIRES — but my hands report all unknown. That's odd: I'm the one who touches the bomb, so if there were tactile features I'd feel them. Maybe the bomb's parts are only perceivable by Deaf (visible: display, light, wire colours) and the manual (Mute). My touch may only matter at the moment of action — I can cut, but the *choice* of wire depends on info from the others.

So the critical path is: Deaf sees → must reach Mute (Mute can hear Deaf's speech? No — Mute cannot speak, but can Mute hear? Mute's row: "Read the manual," cannot speak. Hearing isn't listed as forbidden, so Mute can hear Deaf's speech). Then Mute relays to me by speech. That's the chain: Deaf speaks → Mute hears → Mute speaks to me → I cut.

Deaf has been gesturing at me, which is wasted. Deaf should be *speaking*. I can't tell Deaf directly in words (Deaf can't hear my speech? Deaf cannot hear anything). So I must gesture to Deaf — but Deaf needs to know to *speak* to Mute, and my gesture symbols are opaque unless pre-agreed. This is the coordination problem.

Let me try to establish a simple code with Deaf via gestures, and simultaneously ask Mute to prompt Deaf to speak. Actually Mute can't speak to Deaf either (Deaf can't hear). Hmm. Mute can gesture to Deaf though.

Best move: gesture to Deaf a simple, learnable signal meaning "speak to Mute." But symbols have no inherent meaning until agreed. Still, I can gesture and hope Deaf infers. More productively, speak to Mute asking Mute to gesture to Deaf: "speak, don't gesture at Blind."

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind. Coordination problem: Deaf keeps gesturing at me, but I cannot see gestures — they are blanks. Deaf must SPEAK its observations so you can hear them, then you speak them to me. Please gesture to Deaf telling it to speak aloud to you. Meanwhile tell me anything you already know from the manual.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "👉", "👌"])
```
